spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Five States of Instruction Made Known in the Natural Mind

---

**¶1:**
The five essential states of spiritual instruction that are made known within the natural mind — [GAP-1: REVIEW one] one being called [GAP-2] "peace," which is the interior rest that comes when goods and truths are conjoined and all conflict in the mind ceases; another called "[GAP-3: REVIEW the] silence," [GAP-4] which is the stilling of the natural mind's own activity so that Divine influx may be received without distortion; another "the day," which is the state of full spiritual illumination when the understanding is opened from within; ano[GAP-5: ther] — *the remaining names are lost but the sequence moves from outer tranquility to deeper states of interior reception.*

---

**¶2:**
[GAP-6] The ordering principle that gathers together all scattered goods and truths [GAP-7] shall bring the external person [GAP-8] to renounce all the desires belonging to the natural self-will [GAP-9], causing the external form of life to be brought into conformity with Divine order [GAP-10]. This is the sustaining pathway of Divine truth through which purified good ascends from the lower mind toward the celestial [GAP-11], because [GAP-12] [GAP-13] upward to the [GAP-14] — *the passage describes the column or axis by which goods, once separated from falsities, are elevated progressively through discrete degrees.*

---

**¶3:**
The one they call [GAP-15] — it is the Celestial Human, the primordial Divine Wisdom in human form, who dwells within the containing vessel of living truths [GAP-16] — wisdom from a Divine origin [GAP-17] — who is c[GAP-18: alled] the indwelling Divine Life, that which they have [GAP-19] received in states of heavenly glory [GAP-20]. — *"The ship of living waters" is the doctrinal form that carries and protects celestial good; the First Man dwelling within it is the Divine Human principle from which all regeneration proceeds, borne upon truths that have life in them because they flow from love.*

---

**¶4:**
[GAP-21: cal]l it "day" [GAP-22] — the whole of the spiritual world, the Grand Human, as all things within it shall [GAP-23] be brought into their final order within the infinite Divine state [GAP-24]. Interior truths are extended throughout the Grand Human; it is [GAP-25] the Divine order itself, established in the [GAP-26] celestial kingdom, and the interior life-principles of all who receive influx [GAP-27] — *"Day" here is the universal state of illumination when the Lord's kingdom is fully realized; what is "spread in the universe" are the truths that constitute the connective tissue of the heavenly human form, and the "souls" are the living essences — the will-and-understanding unities — that compose it.*

fills.explanation: The editor's "one" correctly initiates the standard enumeration pattern: "one being called... another called... another..." used throughout the Kephalaia for listing items.

Standard Coptic Kephalaia naming formula where the first item in an enumerated list receives the fuller expression "called by name 'X'" while subsequent items use the shorter "called 'X'" — a well-attested stylistic pattern.
The editor's "the" is confirmed: the definite article parallels the other lesson names — "the peace," "the silence," "the day" — maintaining consistent naming throughout the list.
A simple conjunction connecting the third item in the enumeration, paralleling the comma-separated list structure: "one... another... and another..."
Standard Kephalaia formula for introducing the explanation of a listed item; "As for the gatherer..." begins the didactic exposition of one of the five lessons.

The spiritual reading requires "renouncing desires of the natural self-will"; in Kephalaia register, "to cease from" is the standard formula for renunciation of worldly lusts, corresponding to the stilling of natural activity.
Parallels "the lusts of the world" with a complementary external category: the deeds of the body — matching the spiritual reading's emphasis on conforming the external form of life to Divine order.

A demonstrative pronoun beginning a new identifying sentence: "This is the Pillar of Glory" — standard Kephalaia formula for revealing the identity of a cosmic principle after describing its function.

The spiritual reading describes the Pillar as the pathway through which purified good ascends toward the celestial; in Manichaean natural register, the Pillar of Glory is the column through which light ascends to the realm above.

The "because" clause explains the Pillar's function; "it bears" expresses the Pillar's role of carrying purified elements upward, matching the spiritual sense of progressive elevation through discrete degrees.
Completes the clause "it bears all things up to the [land of light]," expressing the universal scope of the Pillar's gathering and elevating function as described in the spiritual reading.

The destination of ascent through the Pillar of Glory; "land of light" is the standard Kephalaia term for the celestial realm — corresponding to Swedenborg's celestial kingdom toward which purified good ascends.

The spiritual reading identifies this as the Celestial Human borne upon truths flowing from love — in Swedenborg, peace belongs specifically to the celestial kingdom; the First Man dwelling at rest in the ship of living waters is the inmost celestial state of peace.

Connects "living waters" to "light" in a genitive chain: "the ship of living waters of the light" — expressing the spiritual reading's "wisdom from a Divine origin," where the light is the divine source of the living truths.

Transitional formula introducing a secondary name for the First Man: having been identified as 'the peace' (GAP-15), he is "and also" called 'the life' — a standard Kephalaia construction for giving additional epithets to a cosmic figure.

The spiritual reading says "called the indwelling Divine Life"; in Kephalaia natural register, "the life" expresses the living divine principle dwelling within the First Man — the quintessential Manichaean quality of the redeemed celestial being.
The spiritual reading states "that which they have received in states of heavenly glory"; "received" is the standard Kephalaia verb for the appropriation of divine gifts and celestial goods.

Parallels the ¶3 formula "The one they call [name]"; the fill ends with "cal" so that the extant "l" completes "call," yielding "The one they call it 'day'" — a standard Kephalaia identificatory formula.

Creates "the day of the universe" — the spiritual reading identifies this as the universal state of illumination across the whole spiritual world, which in Kephalaia register is "the day of the universe."
Standard Manichaean/Kephalaia eschatological formula: "they shall find rest in the great aeon" — expressing the spiritual reading's "brought into their final order within the infinite Divine state."

The spiritual reading says "interior truths are extended throughout the Grand Human"; in Kephalaia natural register, these are the particles of light spread throughout the cosmos — "The lights that are spread in the universe."

The spiritual reading says "the Divine order itself, established in the celestial kingdom"; in Manichaean natural register, the light spread in the universe IS the divine light that is ultimately established in the aeon — "it is the light established in the aeon of light."

The spiritual reading says "celestial kingdom"; in Kephalaia cosmological vocabulary, "aeon of light" is the standard term for the supreme celestial realm where purified light is permanently established.

The spiritual reading says "the living essences that compose it" — the souls are the constituent beings of the celestial structure; "that dwell therein" expresses their established presence within the aeon of light.
